subject: Incident Retainer Model & Rapid-Triage Bands — pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@brightline.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: peter.sanders@brightline.com
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident retainer model questions

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We talked internally about trying a 6-month pilot for a closer operational SLA for our inference pipelines (primarily inference availability during peak window and an on-call coordination playbook). Two specific questions before we take this to procurement: 

1) Can you price an "incident retainer" variant where we buy fixed rapid-triage slots (e.g., 10 triage hours/month) instead of a pure hourly on-call rate?
2) How does Redwood credit or reconcile incidents that happen during failover (we're worried about double-counting capacity incidents vs infra failover events)?

Attached is our initial runbook excerpt (triage_bands_playbook.xlsx) with the kinds of incidents we'd expect. Can you send a short pricing sketch + a sample retainer addendum for our legal team?

Appreciate it — want to move quickly if the economics make sense.

— Taylor
Taylor Reed
Head of Platform Ops, Brightline Systems
(t) 415-555-0198

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
To: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@brightline.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Sep 2025 10:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident Retainer Model & Rapid-Triage Bands — pricing follow-up

Taylor —

Thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the playbook excerpt. Quick summary of how we typically structure this for pilot customers: 

- Incident retainer: fixed monthly fee that buys a bank of "rapid-triage hours" (used for accelerated investigation, RCA coordination, and prioritized on-call engagement). Hours that exceed the bank are billed at a pre-agreed overtime rate.
- Triage bands: we map incidents to triage bands (P1/P2/P3) with expected response (initial acknowledgement) and target time-to-first-action. The retainer covers faster routing and top-of-queue staffing for P1/P2 inside your peak window.
- Failover reconciliation: we attach incident labeling in the console (auto-tag based on routing & region) and provide incident-level export. For failover events that are infra-triggered, we apply a reconciliation step: if the incident is verified as cloud provider failover (not Redwood-serving logic), we won't credential it against the retainer. If it's a serving runtime regression, it does. We can add a 3rd-party telemetry hook for Brightline so both teams can independently validate.

I'm attaching a sample retainer addendum (incident_retainer_v1.pdf) and a two-scenario pricing sketch below. Rachel, can you confirm model seat/commit assumptions and whether we should propose a 10% pilot discount?

Scenario A — conservative pilot
- 10 triage hours / month retainer: $6,000 / month
- Overtime: $650 / hour after bank
- Includes 24/7 escalation roster with 1-hour SLA to engaged triage engineer during Brightline peak window

Scenario B — higher coverage
- 20 triage hours / month retainer: $10,500 / month
- Overtime: $600 / hour after bank
- Includes weekly runbook syncs + monthly joint RCA workshop

Next steps: if either sketch looks reasonable, we can send a one-page addendum for legal and a short SOW for ops.

Cheers,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

From: rachel.kim@redwood.com
To: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@brightline.com>, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 Oct 2025 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident Retainer Model & Rapid-Triage Bands — pricing follow-up

Hi Taylor —

Couple of practical notes from the pricing side: 

- We can offer a 12% pilot discount if Brightline commits to the 6-month pilot and a short conversion clause (mutual right to convert to a 12-month retainer at a fixed uplift). That would make Scenario A $5,280 / month for the pilot period.
- For billing clarity we'll include a monthly "triage usage" line item (hours consumed, overtime hours, any credits applied).
- For failover reconciliation, we recommend adding a short arbitration clause: incidents tagged as "third-party failover" require a joint sign-off within 10 business days to be excluded. This keeps disputes short.

I can draft the addendum with these three edits (pilot discount, usage line item, arbitration step) and circulate. 

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Director, Pricing & Commercial Ops — Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Taylor Reed <taylor.reed@brightline.com>, rachel.kim@redwood.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Oct 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident Retainer Model & Rapid-Triage Bands — pricing follow-up

Taylor —

One quick engineering clarification to avoid scope creep on the SOW: the triage hours cover Redwood engineering time for diagnostics and prioritized fixes to the serving runtime and routing layer. Activities outside that scope (customer-side config changes, large data migrations, or third-party infra mitigation) will still be billable but we mark them as "adjunct" tasks with separate tracking.

Also, regarding failover detection: we can add a lightweight webhook that pushes a verification artifact (region, node-id, provider event id) to Brightline's incident ticket. That will make the 10-day arbitration much faster since both sides will have the same recorded piece of evidence.

If you give the green light on Scenario A with Rachel's pilot discount, we'll: 
- Circulate a 1-page addendum + SOW draft (legal friendly)
- Schedule a runbook alignment call (30 minutes) to lock the triage band mapping
- Kick trial billing for the pilot month on the agreed start date

Happy to hop on a 20-minute call if you want to walk through the reconciliation flow with my infra lead.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Manager, Reliability — Redwood Inference
